test_title: SSC Selection Post 2025 (Matriculation Level) Official Paper (Held On: 31 Jul, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: The Kailasa Temple at Ellora was built by which ruler?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Krishna I**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Krishna I** (reigned **756–774 CE**) was the successor to **Dantidurga** and a prominent ruler of the **Rashtrakuta Dynasty**. He is the monarch credited with the construction of the magnificent **Kailasa Temple**.
 
• The **Kailasa Temple** is located at **Ellora** (Cave 16) in the **Sambhaji Nagar** (formerly Aurangabad) district of **Maharashtra**. It is one of the most remarkable **monolithic** structures in the world.
 
• The temple is carved out of a single, massive **basalt** cliff. Uniquely, the artisans employed a **top-down** carving method, starting from the summit of the mountain and working downwards to the base.
 
• It is dedicated to **Lord Shiva** and was designed to symbolize **Mount Kailash**, the celestial abode of the deity in the Himalayas.
 
• The construction was an immense engineering feat of the **8th century**, involving the excavation of approximately **200,000 to 400,000 tonnes** of rock over several decades.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Rashtrakuta Dynasty**: 
 
 
• Founded by **Dantidurga** in the **8th century**, this dynasty ruled large parts of the **Deccan** and southern India.
 
• Their capital was located at **Manyakheta**. They were renowned patrons of **art**, **architecture**, and literature, fostering a culture where **Hinduism**, **Buddhism**, and **Jainism** flourished.
 
 
 
• **Ellora Caves**: 
 
 
• A **UNESCO World Heritage Site** since **1983**, it comprises **34 caves** carved into the **Charanandri hills**.
 
• The site includes **12 Buddhist** caves, **17 Hindu** caves, and **5 Jain** caves, reflecting the **religious tolerance** of ancient Indian society.
 
 
 
• **Other Rulers Mentioned**:
 
 
• **Ashoka**: The third **Mauryan Emperor** (**268–232 BCE**) known for spreading **Buddhism** and his **Rock Edicts**. His reign occurred nearly a millennium before the construction of the Kailasa Temple.
 
• **Rajaraja Chola I**: A powerful ruler of the **Chola Empire** (**985–1014 CE**) who built the structural **Brihadeeswarar Temple** at **Thanjavur**, which is distinct from the rock-cut style of Ellora.
 
• **Chandragupta II**: A famous ruler of the **Gupta Dynasty** (c. **375–415 CE**) associated with the **Golden Age** of India. While art flourished under the Guptas, the monolithic Ellora temples belong to the later **Rashtrakuta** period.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Architectural Style**: The temple mainly follows the **Dravidian** architectural style, characterized by a **Vimana** (tower) and a flat-roofed **Mandapa** (pillared hall).
 
• **Sculptural Mastery**: The temple walls feature intricate relief panels, most notably the **Ravana Phadi**, which depicts the demon king **Ravana** attempting to lift **Mount Kailash**.
 
• **Dimensions**: The temple is roughly **32 meters** high, making it one of the largest single monolithic excavations in human history, surpassing even the **Parthenon** in scale.
